removed.reason: Isosceles base angles and the triangle angle sum are Stage 4 skills practised routinely before Stage 5 Paths, so students commonly have them and rehearsal isn't needed.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x+40&=180\\2x&=140\\x&=70\end{align*}$$
The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, and the angles of a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.

removed.reason: Parallel line angle facts are taught and practised in Stage 4 and early Stage 5, so Stage 5 Paths students generally retain them and q4d only uses co-interior angles routinely.

content.prompt: Find the value of each pronumeral.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}z+65&=180\\z&=115\end{align*}$$
$z$ and $65^{\circ}$ are co-interior angles, so they sum to $180^{\circ}$.
